_game: Rush Hour (puzzle: slide cars to free the red car)
_note: Setup: pip install rushhour-gym (in requirements.txt). On first use the package downloads the rushhour-env Go engine of the matching Rush-Hour release into ~/.cache/rushhour-gym/ (checksum-verified); set RUSHHOUR_ENV_BIN or the phase 'binary' field to use a binary of your own, e.g. one built from a checkout with `go build -o rushhour-env ./cmd/rushhour-env`. Env ids: RushHour-v0, RushHour-Easy-v0, RushHourFixed-v0.
_keys_note: Env Discrete(32) is action=slot*2+direction (0=left/up, 1=right/down); slot 0 is always the red car. Humans do not press those indices: curriculum 'keys' are the adapter's meta-actions — 0..3=select up/down/left/right (spatial, what Rush-Hour's gamepad d-pad does), 4/5=select prev/next, 6/7=move back/forward. The defaults below are rushinput.DefaultMap's keyboard: LEFT/RIGHT and 3/4 select prev/next, UP/DOWN and 1/2 (or , .) slide. Select does not call env.step; moves become Discrete and are logged as env_action (-1 for UI-only selects). Keep the message Controls text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_ergonomics_note: White triangles on the selected car show which of its two slides are legal (from the engine action_mask), because a refused move renders identically to a dropped keypress. 'movable_only' (default true, matching Rush-Hour's -movable-only default) makes selection skip cars that cannot move at all. false is Rush-Hour's -movable-only=false: a different task, since noticing which cars are stuck becomes part of the search -- keep it the same across sessions being compared.

text: Slide cars to free the RED car through
LEFT / RIGHT  or  3 / 4   previous / next car
UP    or  1 or ,          slide it left, or up if vertical
DOWN  or  2 or .          slide it right, or down if vertical
White triangles mark the moves a car can make.
